# Same-Input Cross-Engine Dynamics Parity

## Status

Evidence class: software consistency, provisional. This chapter records the
same-input parity pathway of epic #11605 (children P-1 to P-8), so it can be
inventoried. It is not approved. The registry blocker
`UP-D1-same-input-parity-inventory` stays open until UP-D1 inventories the
pathway and a human reviews it. The calculation-level reference, with every
table and receipt hash, is the editable research source
`docs/research/same_input_parity/same_input_parity.tex` (P-9, #11614). It is
separate from this manual.

## Purpose

One full-body specification, driven by the same initial state and the same
joint torques, must produce the same motion in MuJoCo, Drake, Pinocchio,
OpenSim, MyoSuite and Simscape. Agreement shows that the spec-built models are
dynamically identical and that remaining differences come from documented
numerical policy. It says nothing about whether the model matches a human
golfer.

## Conventions

- One specification JSON builds every engine adapter: 44 generalized
  coordinates in spec order, SI units (m, rad, s, N·m).
- The root is a floating base (`TranslationInputX/Y/Z`, `HipInputX/Y/Z`). It is
  unactuated, and root efforts are set to zero.
- The hands are welded to the club by a dual-grip closure. Ground contact uses
  one shared Hunt–Crossley law with common parameters.
- MuJoCo is the reference engine for the trajectory levels.

## Equations

1. Constrained dynamics. With mass matrix $M(q)$, bias
   $h = C(q,v)\,v + g(q)$, efforts $\tau$ and weld rate map $D(q)$ ($D v$ is the
   weld rate residual), the accelerations $a$ and constraint forces $\lambda$
   solve the KKT system
   $$\begin{bmatrix} M & D^{\top} \\ D & 0 \end{bmatrix}
     \begin{bmatrix} a \\ \lambda \end{bmatrix}
     = \begin{bmatrix} \tau - h \\ -\dot{D}\,v \end{bmatrix}$$
   Drake and Pinocchio solve it exactly. MuJoCo adds a $10^{-6}$ Tikhonov term
   by default (`kkt_regularization`); parity runs set it to $0$.
2. Closure projection. Each engine linearises a violated weld in its own frame,
   so raw recorded states are formulation dependent. The convention-free
   correction is the closest point $q^{*}$ on the closure manifold:
   $$q^{*} - q_0 \in \operatorname{row}\!\left(D(q^{*})\right), \qquad
     r(q^{*}) = 0, \qquad v^{*} = v - D^{+} D\, v$$
   It is solved as a fixed point with an inner Newton search (central-difference
   residual Jacobian, step $10^{-7}$). The search stops at
   $\max|r| \le 10^{-13}$, with a cap of 25 iterations, and otherwise raises
   `ArithmeticError`.
3. Integration. Classical RK4 with efforts held zero-order over each step, a
   1 ms step with 8 substeps (effective 0.125 ms) and closure projection after
   every step. A single 1 ms step would amplify the stiff contact modes near
   $-9.9 \times 10^{3}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ by $|R| \approx 274$; 8 substeps bring
   them inside the RK4 stability region.
4. Pointwise gate (L1): $|\Delta a| \le 10^{-6} + 10^{-8} \max|a|$.

## Input Bundle

Schema `same-input-bundle/v1` is exported by the MuJoCo reference and replayed
by every other engine. It holds the spec hash, the closure-consistent
$q_0, v_0$, the per-step efforts $\tau_k$, the contact parameters, the marker
attachments and the integration policy above.

## Acceptance Levels

These numbers are initial. They must not be loosened without a
`Tolerance-Change-Evidence` issue.

| Level | Criterion | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L0, model identity | masses, inertias, frames, $M(q)$ and bias agree to $\le 10^{-9}$ relative | passed |
| L1, pointwise dynamics | constrained accelerations at projected states meet the gate above | passed for MuJoCo, Drake and Pinocchio |
| L2, open-loop trajectory | coordinate error $\le 10^{-6}$ rad and marker error $\le 1$ mm against MuJoCo, or the growth exponent and agreement horizon recorded | passed in 50 ms segments; full horizon recorded |
| L3, closed-loop same controller | the identical tracking controller reproduces the MuJoCo match to $\le 1$ mm | passed for Drake, Pinocchio, OpenSim and MyoSuite |

## Measured Results

Software-consistency results, generated 2026-10-06 on host `brick`. The
receipt hashes and per-frame tables are in the LaTeX reference.

- L0: total mass identical (79.358 kg); $M(q)$ agrees to $9 \times 10^{-13}$
  and the bias to $8 \times 10^{-10}$ N·m.
- L1: all 31 sampled frames pass. The worst projected acceleration difference is
  $1.4 \times 10^{-4}$ rad/s² at a contact spike where $\max|a| \approx 1.3
  \times 10^{5}$ (relative $1.1 \times 10^{-9}$, inside the
  $\epsilon\,\operatorname{cond}(M) \approx 1.4 \times 10^{-7}$ round-off bound).
  At the raw states the difference reaches 41.8 rad/s², which is what the
  projection removes.
- L2 and L3, driver and 7-iron: the worst coordinate error against MuJoCo is
  $\le 1.1 \times 10^{-9}$ rad for Drake and Pinocchio and $\le 7.4 \times
  10^{-12}$ rad for OpenSim. MyoSuite is bit-identical, because it wraps the
  MuJoCo core.
- A single full-horizon open-loop run grows perturbations at 39–41 s⁻¹, so any
  engine pair leaves $10^{-6}$ rad after about 0.5–0.6 s. This is a property
  of the unstable open-loop swing, not an engine disagreement.
- Simscape (P-8, #11613) is pending on the MATLAB R2025b host.

## Failed Experiments

- Raw-state comparison with MuJoCo's default regularisation gave differences up
  to 0.62 rad/s². Removing the regularisation alone was not enough; the closure
  violation had to be projected out.
- Projecting along $D(q_0)$ at the violated state left a $6 \times 10^{-8}$
  state spread between engines. The closest-point version evaluates $D$ on the
  manifold and reduces it to $3 \times 10^{-14}$.
- MJCF `fullinertia` is eigen-decomposed by MuJoCo to only about
  $1.1 \times 10^{-6}$ relative, which produced $3.3 \times 10^{-5}$ rad iron
  errors. The native exporter now emits `diaginertia` and `quat` from numpy
  `eigh`, with a determinant correction that keeps the frame right-handed.

## Tests and Reproduction

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/unit/motion_matching/same_input -m "" -q
MUJOCO_GL=egl PYTHONPATH=.:src python3 -m scripts.same_input_pointwise_parity
```

The first command runs the behavioural tests; engine rows skip where an engine
is not installed. The second rewrites the L1 receipt. The full-swing bundles
and their 16 receipts are reproduced with `scripts/same_input_bundle.py`
(`export`, `replay`, `closed-loop`), as listed in the LaTeX reference.

## Assumptions and Limitations

- Two bundles were compared (one driver, one 7-iron), each from one
  anthropometric spec.
- The compared states are projected onto the grip closure, not the raw
  recorded states.
- The zero-order-hold reference tracks the capture more loosely than the
  canonical pipeline (joint RMS 0.017 versus 0.004 rad). It is a dynamics-parity
  input, not a capture-matching result.
- Contact spikes are ill conditioned ($\operatorname{cond}(M) \approx 6 \times
  10^{8}$), so the relative tolerance is bounded by round-off, not by physics.
- The OpenSim adapter works around two exporter defects (an escaped invalid XML
  element name and a marker set that references a nonexistent `Hub` body).
- The full-swing receipts live outside the repository; only their hashes are
  recorded.
- This is a software-consistency result. It is not scientific qualification
  against capture data, and no uncertainty against an external reference is
  claimed.
